title: Child-care work prevention is higher inside reported utility difficulty, with tenure-specific uncertainty
source_unit: 2025 SIPP public-use file, 2024 reference period; December identified reference-parent person rows with valid annual fall child-care work-prevention status, utility-payment difficulty, and tenure

observations.period: 2024 reference year; utility difficulty and owned/bought tenure

denominator.unit: valid identified reference-parent person records with EWORKMORE, utility, and tenure responses

childcare_prevented_work_or_more.unit: person-weighted percent; Fay-BRR SE 3.107 pp; 95% CI 3.260–15.438

observations.method: December cross-section using WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, G=240, perturbation factor 0.5; EWORKMORE=1 is the numerator.
observations.uncertainty: Small reference-parent record count and wide design-based interval. EWORKMORE describes annual fall child-care arrangements, not December time loss or a dated utility response.
observations.subgroup: ETENURE=1: owned or being bought; EAWBGAS=1: reported utility-payment difficulty.
observations.counterinterpretation: The association may reflect child-care need, work opportunities, household composition, local prices, health, season, or selection into utility difficulty rather than a utility or tenure mechanism.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; utility difficulty and rented tenure

denominator.unit: valid identified reference-parent person records with EWORKMORE, utility, and tenure responses

childcare_prevented_work_or_more.unit: person-weighted percent; Fay-BRR SE 2.430 pp; 95% CI 3.367–12.893

observations.method: December cross-section using WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, G=240, perturbation factor 0.5; EWORKMORE=1 is the numerator.
observations.uncertainty: Small reference-parent record count and wide design-based interval. EWORKMORE is an annual fall-reference measure attached to a December utility condition.
observations.subgroup: ETENURE=2: rented; EAWBGAS=1: reported utility-payment difficulty.
observations.counterinterpretation: A renter-owner comparison does not isolate tenure: provider access, family support, rent burden, job mix, geography, and care need may differ.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; no utility difficulty and owned/bought tenure

denominator.unit: valid identified reference-parent person records with EWORKMORE, utility, and tenure responses

childcare_prevented_work_or_more.unit: person-weighted percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.528 pp; 95% CI 1.801–3.871

observations.method: December cross-section using WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, G=240, perturbation factor 0.5; EWORKMORE=1 is the numerator.
observations.uncertainty: The larger comparison cell is more precise, but the contrast is descriptive and not a counterfactual for utility difficulty.
observations.subgroup: ETENURE=1: owned or being bought; EAWBGAS=2: no reported utility-payment difficulty.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower reported work prevention may reflect different child-care arrangements, work schedules, household structure, or reporting rather than greater room or utility stability.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; no utility difficulty and rented tenure

denominator.unit: valid identified reference-parent person records with EWORKMORE, utility, and tenure responses

childcare_prevented_work_or_more.unit: person-weighted percent; Fay-BRR SE 0.911 pp; 95% CI 3.224–6.796

observations.method: December cross-section using WPFINWGT and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, G=240, perturbation factor 0.5; EWORKMORE=1 is the numerator.
observations.uncertainty: The measure is an annual child-care work-prevention report, not a monthly care allocation or utility consequence; group selection remains uncontrolled.
observations.subgroup: ETENURE=2: rented; EAWBGAS=2: no reported utility-payment difficulty.
observations.counterinterpretation: The renter-owner difference may reflect selection, care need, local labor demand, family support, or housing cost rather than tenure itself.

related_sources.claim: The parent layer supplies the adjacent-month utility, tenure, earnings, and hours transition.
The care layer documents the official EWORKMORE and ETIMELOST universe boundaries.
The official dictionary defines EWORKMORE, EAWBGAS, and ETENURE; the extracted slice exposes ETENURE without a separate ATENURE field.

boundary: This is a descriptive conditional bridge between an annual fall child-care work-prevention report and a December utility/tenure condition. It does not establish a dated bill shock, tenure effect, utility causation, monthly care time, household prevalence, recovery, trust, political action, or a complete material/time/care episode.
